facts.text: MET (Modular Equipment Transporter) was deployed at Fra Mauro during Apollo 14 in 1971.
Nicknamed the 'lunar rickshaw,' this two-wheeled hand cart carried tools, cameras, and sample bags during the EVAs. It was the only wheeled vehicle used before the Lunar Roving Vehicle of Apollo 15.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Enabled astronauts to transport 43 kilograms of lunar samples over rough terrain during two EVAs, more than doubling the sample collection range compared to walking-only missions.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Fra Mauro.
The only human-pulled wheeled vehicle ever used on the Moon; its design informed requirements for the Lunar Roving Vehicle deployed on Apollo 15, 16, and 17.
